help.trust_intro: It's reasonable to be cautious about an unfamiliar open Wi-Fi network. Here's exactly what this device does and doesn't do, verified against its own actual configuration, not just described in general terms.
help.trust_no_https_title: No encryption interception of any kind
help.trust_no_https_body: This device does not run HTTPS at all, on any page - there is no certificate to install, trust, or click through, and no possibility of it intercepting or inspecting encrypted traffic, because it never terminates any. Everything here is a plain local site served over the open Wi-Fi network you already joined.
help.trust_no_cloud_title: No cloud account, no outside service
help.trust_no_cloud_body: Nothing about using this device creates or requires an account anywhere. Every page, file, and reference document is served from this one Raspberry Pi's own local storage - your device talks directly to it, and it talks to nothing else.
help.trust_captive_title: The sign-in prompt is just local navigation
help.trust_captive_body: The "sign in to network" page some devices show automatically is a standard captive-portal redirect, configured to do exactly one thing: bring you to this device's own local home page. It doesn't check credentials, phone home anywhere, or do anything else on your device's behalf.
help.trust_stats_title: Connection counts are aggregate, not per-visitor
help.trust_stats_body: This device keeps a simple hourly count of how many devices are connected - a number, for the operator's own awareness of load - never a list of who connected, when, or for how long. No MAC address, device name, or browsing history is recorded anywhere.
help.trust_id_title: This device's own ID isn't derived from your hardware or its own
help.trust_id_body: The Device ID shown on this page (where present) is a purely random label generated once for this physical unit - not built from any hardware serial number, MAC address, or other identifying value, for this device or yours. Its only purpose is letting a finder or operator refer to "this specific PirateBox" in conversation.
help.trust_content_title: You get exactly what's described, nothing more
help.trust_content_body: Files, Chat, Logbook, Bulletin Board, and the offline Utility Library are the complete list of what this device offers a visitor - there's no hidden functionality reaching further into your device or your traffic than what those features plainly do.
